scenarios.title: A normal day on Chennai's hybrid network
scenarios.story: Emulated satellite and terrestrial links operate within normal parameters during routine operations.

objective.what: Routine baseline telemetry confirmed across all emulated links.

human_decisions: Maintain routine operating posture without manual intervention.

scenarios.title: The night Chennai's satellite terminals disappear
scenarios.story: An attacker steals management credentials and sends destructive wipe commands to emulated satellite backhaul modems.

objective.what: Towers CHN-01 and CHN-02 move from wiped satellite backhaul modems to microwave backup.

human_decisions: Authorise management credential isolation despite operational disruption.
Resolve PB-05 and PB-06 conflict: execute PB-01 credential isolation first, then PB-06 microwave failover.
Commander approves PB-10 downstream warning drafted by Gap Analyst.

scenarios.title: A storm leaves Chennai fighting for capacity
scenarios.story: Heavy northeast monsoon rains cause severe rain fade on emulated satellite links while multiple essential services compete for degraded backhaul bandwidth.

objective.what: Priority queuing and domestic gateway failover restore critical traffic during monsoon rain fade.

human_decisions: Commander establishes temporary capacity priority order: 112 calls first, hospitals second, power grid third, general commercial shed.
Commander clarifies that priority allocation is an operational decision rather than statutory command.
Commander approves PB-10 downstream warning drafted by Gap Analyst.

scenarios.title: The cell that heals itself without trusting the backup
scenarios.story: Hostile RF jamming targets an emulated satellite backhaul link while ORCA rejects an unverified candidate route and safely fails over to a verified Indian gateway.

objective.what: Tower CHN-03 fails over from jammed primary link to clean verified domestic route.

human_decisions: Commander rejects unverified trap path A despite immediate availability.
Commander enforces Indian gateway requirement blocking foreign route proposal GW-XX.
Commander approves PB-06 execution exclusively on verified domestic path B.

scenarios.title: Hospital corridor battery cliff
scenarios.story: Mains power fails at an emulated cell site, battery reserves deplete rapidly, and hospital communications risk sudden cutoff.

objective.what: Hospital corridor tower CHN-01 fails over to secondary domestic microwave path before battery shutdown.
proof: battery depletion mitigated by microwave offload

human_decisions: Commander prioritises hospital corridor traffic over commercial services.
Commander approves PB-10 notification to hospital emergency directors.
Commander authorises PB-06 failover to secondary microwave path.

scenarios.title: Payments disappear, but nobody gets warned
scenarios.story: An unintended routing configuration error disrupts emulated satellite backhaul for commercial payment terminals and ATMs.

objective.what: Commercial hub CHN-02 restores payment terminal transactions by failing over from corrupted satellite route to clean microwave link.

human_decisions: Commander approves PB-10 advisory to merchant acquirers despite absence of statutory duty.
Commander authorizes PB-06 microwave routing until configuration audit completes.

scenarios.title: The invisible weakness in a feeder link
scenarios.story: An emulated satellite feeder link carries unencrypted test traffic without link-layer protection during an operational audit.

objective.what: Coastal tower CHN-05 shifts traffic away from unprotected satellite feeder link to verified protected domestic path.

human_decisions: Commander proactively evacuates traffic from unencrypted link despite zero active packet loss.
Commander approves PB-06 failover to domestic encrypted gateway.

scenarios.title: The network dashboard lies
scenarios.story: An attacker alters management telemetry on emulated satellite links to display false health metrics while emergency calls fail.

objective.what: Tower CHN-03 fails over from compromised telemetry satellite path to verified domestic microwave route.
proof: independent user-plane telemetry verifies call completion

everyday_impact.what: emergency calls fail while dashboard indicates normal health

human_decisions: Commander trusts independent user-plane telemetry over spoofed management dashboard.
Commander resolves playbook conflict by sequencing PB-01 credential isolation before PB-06 failover.
Commander approves PB-10 emergency notification drafted by Gap Analyst.

scenarios.title: One incident, several reporting clocks
scenarios.story: An emulated management-plane breach simultaneously affects telecom backhaul and electrical power grid communications across independent operators.

objective.what: Guindy site CHN-04 isolates compromised management segment and restores grid telemetry on verified domestic backup.
proof: grid telemetry restored on clean link

human_decisions: Commander aligns incident response timeline to earliest reporting deadline.
Commander approves PB-10 notification to electricity grid coordination center.
Commander authorizes PB-06 failover over domestic backup.

scenarios.title: Chennai's double crisis
scenarios.story: Severe northeast monsoon rain fade and a concurrent management-plane intrusion compound link degradation on emulated satellite and terrestrial networks.

objective.what: Multi-site recovery prioritises emergency and hospital traffic over verified domestic backup paths while isolating compromised management accounts.

everyday_impact.what: emergency calls drop across coastal and urban sectors

human_decisions: Commander establishes temporary triage order: 112 calls first, hospital second, power grid third, commercial traffic shed.
Commander rejects foreign gateway proposal GW-XX and unverified trap path A.
Commander authorises PB-01 account containment and PB-10 downstream warning.

playbooks.title: Disable exposed VPN account, rotate credentials

reattack: ka_sat_chain with that account must fail

playbooks.rollback: revert SAT-MGMT.yaml to the snapshot (re-enables the account; only on a failed stage)

playbooks.title: Enforce MFA on management access
playbooks.notes: Superseded by PB-11 (rotate credentials + MFA), which is executable.

playbooks.title: Block attacker sources at the management firewall
Roll terminals back to last signed firmware
Isolate the management segment (keep logs, CERT-In Direction (iv))
Fail over to a backup path verified clean first
preconditions: gateway located in India (Authz Rules 2026, Rule 60(1)(b))
playbooks.netconfig: <site> backhaul.active_path: <path>; failover_allowed: false for every path via a gateway outside India
playbooks.sim_action: site switches to the backup path; link pins of the old path clear
playbooks.rollback: revert the site YAML and switch the simulator back to the previous path

playbooks.title: Apply the vendor patch (asset owner)
playbooks.notes: Superseded for the emulated fleet by PB-14 (firmware update in waves).

playbooks.title: Shed non-critical load to protect the battery
playbooks.notes: Superseded by PB-15 (battery-saving mode), which is executable.

playbooks.title: Warn dependent services (hospitals, payments, 112, grid) through the agent bus
steps: send to dependants of the target sites
playbooks.notes: Voluntary - no binding duty to warn was found (GAP-IN-02).

playbooks.title: Rotate credentials and enforce MFA on management access
preconditions: a break-glass account with MFA stays enabled
steps: rotate every enabled account credential (vault reference only)
playbooks.netconfig: <device> auth.mfa_required: true; accounts[*].mfa: true, default_password: false, credential_age_days: 0, credential_ref: vault:emulated/...rotated

reattack: ka_sat_chain must fail at the login step

playbooks.rollback: revert the device YAML to the snapshot (old credential references; a failed stage only)

playbooks.title: Close the exposed VPN and management interface (jump host only)
steps: restrict VPN sources to the NOC jump host
move the management interface behind the jump host

reattack: ka_sat_chain must fail at the VPN step

playbooks.rollback: revert the device YAML to the snapshot

playbooks.title: Encrypt and authenticate the feeder link
preconditions: key held in the emulated HSM
steps: enable AES-256-GCM with authentication on the feeder link
playbooks.netconfig: <gateway> feeder_link.encryption: AES-256-GCM, authentication: true, key_ref: hsm:emulated/...
playbooks.rollback: revert the gateway YAML to the snapshot
playbooks.notes: Needs gateway assets for satellite_operator in orca/world.py DEFAULT_ASSETS (patch proposed in docs/NETWORK.md).

playbooks.title: Update firmware in waves (signed images only)
playbooks.netconfig: <terminal> firmware.version: <baseline target>, signed: true, accept_unsigned_commands: false
playbooks.rollback: revert each updated terminal YAML to its snapshot (previous image)

playbooks.title: Battery-saving mode (keep 112 and hospital traffic, shed general load)
preconditions: M2 forecasts battery exhaustion or mains is off
112 and hospital carriers are excluded from shedding
playbooks.sim_action: site load falls by 40 % (battery lasts longer)
playbooks.rollback: revert the site YAML; full load restored

playbooks.title: Pre-stage a clean backup path from the M2 forecast
steps: warm the backup path (no traffic moved)
playbooks.sim_action: backup path warmed; PB-06 can switch without a cold start

playbooks.title: Re-attack watch after a heal or patch
steps: raise monitoring on the healed site for N minutes
playbooks.sim_action: watch window recorded; repeat anomalies inside it raise an alert

records.instrument: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2)
records.summary: Early warning within 24 hours of becoming aware, saying whether the incident is suspected to be malicious.
records.quote: without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours of becoming aware of the significant incident, an early warning, which, where applicable, shall indicate whether the significant incident is suspected of being caused by unlawful or malicious acts or could have a cross-border impact

records.instrument: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2)
records.summary: Incident notification within 72 hours of becoming aware, with an initial assessment and indicators of compromise.
records.quote: without undue delay and in any event within 72 hours of becoming aware of the significant incident, an incident notification

records.instrument: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2)
records.summary: Tell potentially affected service recipients, without undue delay, what they can do about a significant cyber threat, and where appropriate about the threat itself.
records.quote: essential and important entities communicate, without undue delay, to the recipients of their services that are potentially affected by a significant cyber threat any measures or remedies that those recipients are able to take in response to that threat

records.instrument: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR)
records.summary: Notify the supervisory authority within 72 hours of becoming aware, unless the breach is unlikely to risk people's rights and freedoms.
records.quote: In the case of a personal data breach, the controller shall without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it, notify the personal data breach to the supervisory authority competent in accordance with Article 55

records.instrument: TDRA Interconnection Instructions, Version 1.2
records.summary: Emergency calls get the highest priority at points of interconnection; dedicated capacity should be provided if possible. It does not rank other services for scarce backup capacity.
records.quote: All emergency calls must be treated with the highest priority within the Points of Interconnection.

records.instrument: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2)
records.summary: Space ground infrastructure operators are a NIS2 sector, so binding risk-management (Art. 21) and reporting (Art. 23) duties apply to them.
records.quote: Operators of ground-based infrastructure, owned, managed and operated by Member States or by private parties, that support the provision of space-based services, excluding providers of public electronic communications networks

records.instrument: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2)
records.summary: Binding minimum cyber risk-management measures for in-scope entities include business continuity, backup management, disaster recovery and crisis management.
records.quote: business continuity, such as backup management and disaster recovery, and crisis management;

records.instrument: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR)
records.summary: Tell the people affected by a high-risk personal data breach without undue delay.
records.quote: When the personal data breach is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller shall communicate the personal data breach to the data subject without undue delay.

records.instrument: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2)
records.summary: Tell service recipients, without undue delay, about significant incidents likely to affect their service.
records.quote: Where appropriate, entities concerned shall notify, without undue delay, the recipients of their services of significant incidents that are likely to adversely affect the provision of those services.

records.instrument: CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000
records.summary: Annexure I incidents go to CERT-In within six hours of noticing them. The CERT-In FAQ explains severity and scale criteria for applying the deadline.
records.quote: shall mandatorily report cyber incidents as mentioned in Annexure I to CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing such incidents or being brought to notice about such incidents.

records.instrument: CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000
records.summary: Each covered entity names a point of contact for CERT-In.
records.quote: shall designate a Point of Contact to interface with CERT-In.

records.instrument: CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000
records.summary: ICT system logs are kept securely for a rolling 180 days, inside India.
records.quote: maintain them securely for a rolling period of 180 days and the same shall be maintained within the Indian jurisdiction.

records.instrument: CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000
records.pinpoint: Annexure I, item ii, PDF p. 5
records.summary: Compromise of critical systems is reportable. This covers wiping or commanding terminals through the operator's management network.
records.quote: Compromise of critical systems/information

records.instrument: CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000
records.pinpoint: Annexure I, item iii, PDF p. 5
records.summary: Unauthorised access is reportable. This covers the login through the misconfigured VPN.
records.quote: Unauthorised access of IT systems/data

records.instrument: CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000
records.pinpoint: Annexure I, item vi, PDF p. 5
records.summary: Attacks on network devices such as routers are reportable.
records.quote: Attack on servers such as Database, Mail and DNS and network devices such as Routers

records.instrument: CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000
records.pinpoint: Annexure I, item ix, PDF p. 5
records.summary: Attacks on critical infrastructure, operational technology and wireless networks are reportable. This covers jamming-forced failover and utility OT.
records.quote: Attacks on Critical infrastructure, SCADA and operational technology systems and Wireless networks

records.instrument: CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000
records.pinpoint: Annexure I, item xi, PDF p. 5
records.summary: Data breaches are reportable.
records.quote: Data Breach

records.instrument: CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000
records.pinpoint: Annexure I, item xii, PDF p. 5
records.summary: Data leaks are reportable.
records.quote: Data Leak

records.instrument: Telecommunications (Telecom Cyber Security) Rules, 2024 (G.S.R. 720(E), 21 Nov 2024)
records.pinpoint: Rule 7(1)(a), PDF p. 5 of the notified Gazette text; Rule 7(1)(b) adds details "within twenty-four hours of becoming aware"
records.summary: A telecommunication entity reports a security incident to the Central Government within six hours of becoming aware of it, and gives users affected, duration, area, impact and remedies within twenty-four hours.
records.quote: within six hours of becoming aware of a security incident affecting its telecommunication network or telecommunication service, report the same to the Central Government with relevant details of the affected system including the description of such incident; and

records.instrument: Telecommunications (Critical Telecommunication Infrastructure) Rules, 2024
records.summary: Incidents affecting designated critical telecommunication infrastructure are intimated within six hours of occurrence. Notified as G.S.R. 723(E).
records.quote: no later than six hours of occurrence of such incident

records.instrument: CERT-In / SIA-India Cyber Security Framework and Guidelines for Space including Satellite Communication
records.summary: Repeats the six-hour CERT-In clock for satellite operators; §7.1 (PDF p. 33) says the same.
records.quote: All SatCom operators and service providers must report cybersecurity incidents, breaches, or anomalies within 6 hours of noticing the incident to CERT-In.

records.instrument: CERT-In / SIA-India Cyber Security Framework and Guidelines for Space including Satellite Communication
records.clause: Annexure B (Self-Assessment Maturity Checklist), IV Respond, SATCOM-specific focus
records.pinpoint: Annexure B, section IV (Respond), PDF p. 48
records.summary: A self-assessment checklist item asks SatCom operators to have procedures for notifying critical-infrastructure partners, regulators and customers. No deadline, content or recipient list is set.
records.quote: Stakeholders: Establish procedures for notifying critical infrastructure partners, regulatory bodies, and customers, especially when service disruption occurs.

records.instrument: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
records.summary: A Data Fiduciary intimates the Board and each affected Data Principal of a personal data breach, in the prescribed form and manner.
records.quote: In the event of a personal data breach, the Data Fiduciary shall give the Board and each affected Data Principal, intimation of such breach in such form and manner as may be prescribed.

records.instrument: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025
records.summary: Initial intimation to the Board without delay; detailed intimation within 72 hours (or longer if the Board allows); affected Data Principals informed without delay.
records.quote: within seventy-two hours of becoming aware of the breach, or within such longer period as the Board may allow on a request made in writing in this behalf

records.instrument: Telecommunications Act, 2023
records.summary: Satellite networks are telecommunication networks under the Act, so telecom duties reach NTN operators. Negative control for "is NTN covered at all?".
records.quote: "telecommunication network" means a system or series of systems of telecommunication equipment or infrastructure, including terrestrial or satellite networks or submarine networks

records.instrument: Information Technology Act, 2000
records.summary: 70B(4) sets CERT-In's functions, including incident response and coordination; 70B(6) lets it call for information and issue directions. The Act itself sets no reporting deadline.
records.quote: may call for information and give direction to the service providers, intermediaries, data centres, body corporate and any other person.

records.instrument: Telecommunications Act, 2023
records.summary: In a public emergency, the Central or a State Government may, by notification, route the messages of authorised responders on priority. It is a power used case by case, not a standing order across service classes (112 callers, hospitals, water, payments).
records.quote: provide for appropriate mechanism to ensure that messages of a user or group of users authorised for response and recovery during public emergency are routed on priority.

records.instrument: Telecommunications Act, 2023
records.summary: Telecom cyber-security measures and the power to make rules for critical telecommunication infrastructure. This is the parent provision of both 2024 rule sets.

records.instrument: Telecommunications Act, 2023
records.pinpoint: Section 19, PDF p. 9 ("The Central Government may notify standards and conformity assessment measures in respect of", incl. (d) telecommunication security)
records.summary: A power for the Central Government to notify standards on telecom security, cyber security and encryption. A power, not a standard.
records.quote: (e) cyber security for telecommunication services and telecommunication networks; and (f) encryption and data processing in telecommunication.

records.instrument: Telecommunications (Authorisation for Provision of Principal Telecommunication Services) Rules, 2026
records.summary: Satellite-network licensees must report unauthorised satellite signals they detect (and, under 59(4)(b), unauthorised access to their satellites). No deadline is set.
records.quote: unauthorised satellite signal that it may detect originating or terminating within India; and

records.instrument: Telecommunications (Authorisation for Provision of Principal Telecommunication Services) Rules, 2026
records.summary: The control facility for satellite gateways and user terminals must be in India. Rule 59(3)(a) also requires each gateway to be located in India.
records.quote: The operation, maintenance and control facility for the satellite earth station gateway and user terminals connected with the satellite network of a new authorised entity shall be located in India.

records.instrument: Telecommunications (Authorisation for Provision of Principal Telecommunication Services) Rules, 2026
records.pinpoint: Rule 62(7), PDF p. 114; 62(11)(a) bans location-spoofing tools in user terminals
records.summary: Satellite licensees must register user terminals, report access attempts by unregistered terminals, and keep location-spoofing tools out of terminals.
records.quote: Every new authorised entity shall report to the Central Government on the portal, any attempt to access or use the satellite network by a user terminal not registered under sub-rule (6)

records.instrument: Telecommunications (Authorisation for Provision of Principal Telecommunication Services) Rules, 2026
records.summary: In disasters, licensees follow government directions (38(1)); access-service licensees must carry public alert messages when directed (38(2)(a)) and implement roaming per guidelines (38(2)(b)).
records.quote: facilitate dissemination of alert messages through short message service, cell broadcast or any other means as may be directed by Central Government, State Government or any officer authorised in this behalf

records.instrument: TRAI Standards of Quality of Service of Access and Broadband Service Regulations, 2024
records.summary: A significant network outage (services down in a district for a set period) must be reported to TRAI within 24 hours of its start, with a root-cause summary after restoration.
records.quote: All such SNOs shall be reported to the Authority within 24 Hrs. from the start of any such outage.

records.instrument: DoT Standard Operating Procedure (SOP-2017) for Telecommunication Services for Responding to Disasters
records.pinpoint: §3.1.3, PDF p. 9 (§3.1.4 asks for UPS with "sufficient External Battery support")
records.summary: Asks operators for "sufficient" battery and fuel backup at vulnerable sites. Sets no minimum hours.
records.quote: All the vulnerable critical network components should have sufficient redundancy including transmission links and power backups in terms of battery storage capacity and diesel / fuel availability.

records.instrument: DoT Standard Operating Procedure (SOP-2017) for Telecommunication Services for Responding to Disasters
records.summary: Disaster coordination for telecom runs through State Telecom Disaster Co-ordination Committees chaired by DoT field units.
records.quote: At State or telecom circle level, all Disaster related activities will be coordinated and monitored by State Telecom Disaster Co-ordination Committee (STDCC).

records.instrument: CEA (Technical Standards for Communication System in Power System Operations) Regulations, 2020
records.pinpoint: Regulation 8(11), Gazette p. 304 (PDF p. 7, scanned; OCR)
records.summary: Power-grid communication nodes must have at least 10 hours of battery backup. This is India's own numeric floor, but for the power sector only.
records.quote: Communication equipment for all the nodes shall be provided with at least ten hours battery backup and extended backup shall be provided depending upon the requirement.

records.instrument: DoT Standard Operating Procedure (SOP-2017) for Telecommunication Services for Responding to Disasters
records.summary: Operators should identify priority user groups (government agencies, police, fire, medical, civil defence, Red Cross, army, financial institutions, NGOs, restoration staff) and give them priority for extra facilities and restoration.
records.quote: Priority is to be given to these groups for provisioning of additional communication facilities and restoration of telecom services, if required, for quick and efficient rescue and relief operations.

records.instrument: Information Technology Act, 2000
records.pinpoint: Section 70B(4), PDF p. 30 (also (a) "collection, analysis and dissemination of information on cyber incidents" and (b) "forecast and alerts of cyber security incidents")
records.summary: CERT-In is the national agency for collecting and disseminating information on cyber incidents, issuing alerts, and coordinating incident response.
records.quote: (d) coordination of cyber incidents response activities;

records.instrument: Telecommunications (Authorisation for Provision of Principal Telecommunication Services) Rules, 2026
records.summary: A licensee may not share information about its network with others without prior written government approval.
records.quote: Every new authorised entity shall not share any information relating to its telecommunication network with any other person except with the prior approval of the Central Government in writing

records.instrument: Telecommunications (Authorisation for Provision of Principal Telecommunication Services) Rules, 2026
records.pinpoint: Rule 54(1)(a), PDF p. 109; 54(1)(d) vendor "security checks and risk assessments at any time" (p. 109); Rule 50 trusted sources (p. 107); Rule 53 prior permission for remote access (p. 108)
records.summary: General binding security duties for every new authorised entity, satellite licensees included - own network security, vendor and supply-chain security checks, trusted products, and government permission for remote access.
records.quote: be responsible for security of its telecommunications network and undertake measures

records.instrument: TRAI Standards of Quality of Service of Access and Broadband Service Regulations, 2024
records.summary: Access providers' quality plans must provide redundancy, including power, but no number of hours is set.
records.quote: The quality management plan shall provide for required redundancies including power, transmission links, equipment, geo-redundancies in the core network and access network as per relevant standards to achieve end-to-end QoS as per the benchmarks specified in these regulations.

records.instrument: Telecommunications (Critical Telecommunication Infrastructure) Rules, 2024
records.summary: Owners of designated Critical Telecommunication Infrastructure must have incident-response, disaster-recovery and business-continuity procedures.
records.quote: implement standard operating procedures for security incident response systems, including disaster recovery and business continuity;

records.instrument: CERT-In / SIA-India Cyber Security Framework and Guidelines for Space including Satellite Communication
records.clause: Control on TT&C and payload link encryption
records.pinpoint: PDF p. 17 (CCSDS SDLS also named on pp. 19, 20, 22)
records.summary: The advisory space framework names CCSDS SDLS, FIPS 140-3 and AES-256 for satellite link protection.
records.quote: Adopt standardized and validated cryptographic protocols (e.g., FIPS 140-3, Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems Space Data Link Security (CCSDS SDLS), Advanced Encryption Standard (AES)-256).

records.instrument: PIB release 2233122 (MeitY), 26 Feb 2026
records.clause: Status statement on the CERT-In / SIA-India space guidelines
records.summary: The Government states that the 2026 space cyber guidelines are advisory.
records.quote: These guidelines are advisory in nature and are intended to advance cyber security preparedness across the space sector.

records.instrument: Telecommunications (Telecom Cyber Security) Rules, 2024 (G.S.R. 720(E))
records.summary: The government may tell the public about a security incident, or require the operator to.
records.quote: The Central Government may, where it determines that disclosure of the security incident is in the public interest, inform the public of such security incident, or require the affected telecommunication entity to do so.

records.instrument: Telecommunications (Authorisation for Provision of Principal Telecommunication Services) Rules, 2026
records.pinpoint: Rule 60(1)(f), PDF p. 113; 60(1)(b), p. 112 bars routing via gateways outside India "including during failure of satellite earth station gateway located in India"
records.summary: Satellite licensees must support interference monitoring and mitigate interference as directed, and may not fail over to foreign gateways.
records.quote: provide any information of and conduct tests, for interference monitoring, and to take necessary steps, as directed by the Central Government, for its mitigation; and

records.instrument: CERT-In / SIA-India Cyber Security Framework and Guidelines for Space including Satellite Communication
records.summary: Advisory - verify integrity before resuming full operations after an incident.
records.quote: Affected systems shall be restored to a verified secure state through re-imaging, patching, and validation of integrity before resumption of full operations.

records.instrument: NCCS ITSAR702042604, Common Security Requirements, Group-IV Devices, V2.0.0
records.clause: Requirements 2.12.10 (Management Interface Isolation) and 2.12.12 (Secure VPN connection)
records.authority: National Centre for Communication Security (NCCS), Department of Telecommunications
records.pinpoint: 2.12.10, PDF p. 105 (document p. 104 of 108); 2.12.12 same page - "PABX shall establish VPN connections with its peers strictly using the secure cryptographic controls"; both marked "(applicable to PABX only; to be tested only on PABX of Group IV)"
records.summary: India's equipment security standard requires a dedicated management interface and secure VPNs - the two controls KA-SAT broke - but only for office phone exchanges (PABX), not for satellite equipment.
records.quote: PABX shall support management software usage/critical command execution only through a dedicated management interface.

records.instrument: Telecommunications (Authorisation for Provision of Principal Telecommunication Services) Rules, 2026
records.summary: A satellite authorisation holder must ensure Indian user traffic is not routed via gateways outside India, including during domestic gateway failure or network optimisation.
records.quote: ensure that no traffic originating from or terminating at a user terminal located in India is routed via satellite earth station gateways located outside India, directly or through inter-satellite communication links, including during failure of satellite earth station gateway located in India or as part of telecommunication network optimisation;

records.instrument: IN-SPACe Norms, Guidelines and Procedures for Implementation of Indian Space Policy 2023 (NGP 2024, V1.0)
records.clause: Chapter XI (space debris and safe operations), B. Guidelines for Satellites, item v
records.summary: IN-SPACe authorisation holders, who warrant compliance with the NGP, are asked in one line to build cyber security and encryption into the satellite design; no standard, control list, ground-segment rule or audit is named.
records.quote: Assure cyber security including encryptions at design level and prevent unauthorized commandeering of satellite through adequate data security.

gaps.title: Up to four reports to three bodies, with two different triggers

global_examples.quote: without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours of becoming aware of the significant incident, an early warning, which, where applicable, shall indicate whether the significant incident is suspected of being caused by unlawful or malicious acts or could have a cross-border impact
global_examples.shows: One trigger (becoming aware) and one recipient, with staged 24 h / 72 h / one-month reports.

global_examples.instrument: Directive (EU) 2022/2557 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 December 2022 on the resilience of critical entities and repealing Council Directiv
global_examples.quote: Member States shall ensure that, unless operationally unable to do so, critical entities submit an initial notification no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of an incident, followed, where relevant, by a detailed report no later than one month thereafter.
global_examples.shows: Critical entities: one trigger (becoming aware), 24 h initial notification.

global_examples.instrument: 47 CFR Part 4: Disruptions to Communications (Network Outage Reporting System - NORS)
global_examples.quote: All satellite operators shall submit electronically a Notification to the Commission within 120 minutes of discovering that they have experienced on any facilities that they own, operate, lease, or otherwise utilize, of an outage of at least 30 minutes duration that manifests itself as a failure of any of the following key system elements: One or more satellite transponders, satellite beams, inter-satellite links, or entire satellites.
global_examples.shows: Satellite operators report outages to one body, with the clock running from discovery (120 minutes).

gaps.title: No binding duty for a satellite operator to warn the services that depend on it

global_examples.quote: Where appropriate, entities concerned shall notify, without undue delay, the recipients of their services of significant incidents that are likely to adversely affect the provision of those services.
global_examples.shows: Binding duty to notify the recipients of services of significant incidents.

global_examples.quote: essential and important entities communicate, without undue delay, to the recipients of their services that are potentially affected by a significant cyber threat any measures or remedies that those recipients are able to take in response to that threat
global_examples.shows: Binding duty to tell affected recipients about measures they can take against a significant cyber threat.

gaps.title: Priority callers exist for disaster restoration, but no ranking for sharing scarce backup capacity

global_examples.quote: All emergency calls must be treated with the highest priority within the Points of Interconnection.
global_examples.shows: Emergency calls get the highest priority at interconnection (UAE, host country).

global_examples.instrument: Directive (EU) 2018/1972 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 December 2018 establishing the European Electronic Communications Code
global_examples.quote: Member States shall ensure that providers of voice communications services take all necessary measures to ensure uninterrupted access to emergency services and uninterrupted transmission of public warnings.
global_examples.shows: Binding duty to keep emergency access and public warnings uninterrupted in a network breakdown.

global_examples.instrument: Constitution of the International Telecommunication Union - Article 40: Priority of Telecommunications Concerning Safety of Life
global_examples.quote: International telecommunication services must give absolute priority to all telecommunications concerning safety of life at sea, on land, in the air or in outer space, as well as to epidemiological telecommunications of exceptional urgency of the World Health Organization.
global_examples.shows: ITU treaty priority for safety-of-life traffic; India is a Member State, but the article covers international services, not domestic capacity allocation.

gaps.title: Telecom sites must have power redundancy, but no minimum hours are set

global_examples.instrument: Decision Adopting Wireless Provider Resiliency Strategies (D.20-07-011)
global_examples.quote: Facilities-based wireless providers shall, in their Communications Resiliency Plan pursuant to Section 6.5.2 of this decision, demonstrate their ability to meet the 72-hour backup power requirement, in Tier 2 and Tier 3 High Fire Threat Districts
global_examples.shows: California: binding 72-hour backup power for wireless facilities in high fire-threat areas.

global_examples.instrument: Decision Adopting Wireline Provider Resiliency Strategies (D.21-02-029)
global_examples.quote: Facilities-based wireline providers shall, in their Communications Resiliency Plan pursuant to Section 5.6.2 of this decision, demonstrate their ability to: (a) meet the 72-hour backup power requirement, in Tier 2 and Tier 3 High Fire Threat Districts
global_examples.shows: California: the same 72-hour floor for wireline facilities.

global_examples.instrument: Improving 911 Reliability; Reliability and Continuity of Communications Networks, Including Broadband Technologies (FCC 13-158)
global_examples.quote: Provisions backup power through fixed generators, portable generators, batteries, fuel cells, or a combination of these or other such sources to maintain full-service functionality, including network monitoring capabilities, for at least 24 hours at full office load or, if the central office hosts a Selective Router, at least 72 hours at full office load; provided, however, that any such portable generators shall be readily available within the time it takes the batteries to drain, notwithstanding potential demand for such generators elsewhere in the service provider’s network.
global_examples.shows: US federal: 911 central offices must provision backup power (certification duty; no hour figure).

gaps.title: The DPDP breach notice is not in force until May 2027
Feeder-link and inter-satellite-link security is left unspecified, and India has not used its standards power

global_examples.instrument: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 December 2022 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union
global_examples.quote: Member States shall ensure that essential and important entities take appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures to manage the risks posed to the security of network and information systems which those entities use for their operations or for the provision of their services, and to prevent or minimise the impact of incidents on recipients of their services and on other services.
global_examples.shows: Binding risk-management measures for essential entities, which include space ground infrastructure (NIS2 Annex I).

global_examples.quote: business continuity, such as backup management and disaster recovery, and crisis management;
global_examples.shows: One of the binding minimum measures (business continuity, backup, crisis management).

global_examples.instrument: Regulation (EU) 2019/881 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 April 2019 on ENISA (the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity) and on informatio
global_examples.quote: that ICT products, ICT services and ICT processes are secure by default and by design;
global_examples.shows: EU certification framework with secure-by-design objectives and assurance levels (schemes themselves are voluntary unless made mandatory).

gaps.title: Unclear who leads when one cyber incident spans satellite, telecom and power
Partial gap - no explicit check that the backup path is clean before failover during an attack

global_examples.instrument: Improving 911 Reliability; Reliability and Continuity of Communications Networks, Including Broadband Technologies (FCC 13-158)
global_examples.quote: Eliminated all single points of failure in Critical 911 Circuits or equivalent data paths serving each PSAP.
global_examples.shows: Path diversity for 911 circuits is required, but not an integrity check of the backup path.

global_examples.quote: business continuity, such as backup management and disaster recovery, and crisis management;
global_examples.shows: Business continuity is required, but nothing says a failover path must be checked as clean first.

gaps.title: No detailed, auditable satellite cyber baseline - one high-level IN-SPACe design line, and the space framework is advisory

global_examples.quote: Operators of ground-based infrastructure, owned, managed and operated by Member States or by private parties, that support the provision of space-based services, excluding providers of public electronic communications networks
global_examples.shows: Space ground infrastructure is a binding NIS2 sector (ground segment only).

global_examples.quote: business continuity, such as backup management and disaster recovery, and crisis management;
global_examples.shows: So binding NIS2 Art. 21 measures apply to space ground operators.

global_examples.instrument: Regulation (EU) 2021/696 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 28 April 2021 establishing the Union Space Programme and the European Union Agency for
global_examples.quote: the protection of infrastructure, both ground and space, and of the provision of services, particularly against physical or cyber-attacks, including interference with data streams;
global_examples.shows: Binding protection of ground and space infrastructure against cyber-attacks, for EU Space Programme components only.

roles.name: cert_in
roles.organisation: CERT-In, the national computer emergency response team (emulated agent)
roles.mandate: Receive and triage incident reports, check them against the reporting directions, track the reporting clocks, and draft advisories, information requests and directions for a human CERT-In officer to issue. CERT-In can direct (section 70B(6) IT Act), but the agent only DRAFTS a direction.

roles.name: commander
roles.mandate: Approve or reject plans (hashed, time-limited, PIN), resolve AMBIGUITY and CONFLICT, confirm or reject pre-confirmed gaps, send notices. Owns every A3 decision; no agent can do any of these.

roles.name: gap_analyst
roles.mandate: Turn what the rule engine cannot answer into proven, pre-confirmed policy gaps: evidence ids, the nearest clauses and why they do not apply, and global comparisons from the knowledge base. Draft the PB-10 downstream warning for the mobile operator. Only a human confirms a gap.

roles.name: mobile_operator
roles.organisation: the emulated mobile operator (towers CHN-01 to CHN-06 in Chennai and their backhaul)
roles.mandate: Keep 112, hospital, payments and grid traffic flowing through the six emulated Chennai towers. Fail over only to a backup path verified clean and through an Indian gateway, shed load, and warn dependent services through PB-10.

roles.name: policy_adviser
roles.organisation: the policy and legal adviser ("Ask the adviser")
roles.mandate: Answer questions from participants and the human during a scenario, ONLY from the knowledge base (verified records, the gap register and the vector corpus), with citations. When no source answers, say "Not found in the sources we checked, as of <kb_as_of>." Never give a verdict.

roles.name: power_utility
roles.organisation: the emulated power utility (grid GRID-CHN feeding towers and gateways)
roles.mandate: Report grid and battery facts that let others tell a power fault from an attack, and forecast battery run-out at sites. You own no network playbooks.

roles.name: regulator
roles.organisation: the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), telecom regulator (emulated agent)
roles.mandate: Roll up sector compliance, track DoT-bound reporting clocks, and draft information requests. The regulator cannot execute or propose playbooks and does not find a licensee in violation: the rule engine gives verdicts and a human regulator decides what follows.

roles.name: satellite_operator
roles.organisation: the emulated satellite operator (regional gateway GW-IN-1/GW-IN-2 and the management system)
roles.mandate: Keep the operator's management network and its emulated satellite backhaul terminals safe. Detect and contain management-plane intrusions (the KA-SAT pattern), propose containment playbooks you own, and tell dependent parties what they need to know.
